title: Experimental Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key distribution with Flawed State-Preparation over 300 km
authors: Yi-Fei Lu, Yan-Yang Zhou, Yang Wang, Yu Zhou, Xiao-Lei Jiang, Xin-Hang Li, Hai-Tao Wang, Yan-Mei Zhao, Jia-Ji Li, Chun Zhou, Hong-Wei Li, Lin-Jie Zhou, Wan-Su Bao
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) promises theoretically secure communication. However, it encounters challenges in implementation security and performance due to inevitable device imperfections. Since the proposal of measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD, the critical step toward practical security is to secure QKD with imperfect sources. The source imperfections manifest as state-preparation uncertainty (SPU) in various aspects, e.g., encoding uncertainty, intensity fluctuation, and imperfect vacuum states. Here, we perform an MDI-QKD experiment and achieve both high practical security and superior performance. We address the general form of SPU and guarantee a tight estimation of the secret key rate based on the operator dominance method. We achieve secure key distribution over 303.37 km, which not only represents the farthest distance in experiments involving SPU but also considers the most SPU scenarios. Our experimental results represent a significant step toward promoting practical and secure quantum communication.
summary: This paper reports an experimental MDI-QKD system that successfully maintains high security and performance over distances exceeding 300 km. The key innovation is the rigorous incorporation of State-Preparation Uncertainty (SPU) into the security analysis using the operator dominance method. This work significantly advances the practical feasibility of long-haul quantum communication networks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing secure Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) when quantum sources are imperfect, specifically by accounting for State-Preparation Uncertainty (SPU).
main_result: The authors achieved a record secure key distribution distance of over 300 km while rigorously accounting for the general form of SPU, demonstrating robust performance.
method: They utilized the operator dominance method to derive tight theoretical bounds and performed a complex MDI-QKD experiment involving characterization of phase and intensity fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system is an experimental Measurement-Device-Independent QKD (MDI-QKD) setup using free-running continuous-wave lasers at 1550.12 nm. Encoding uses time-bin and phase encoding, and the setup includes multiple modulators and single-photon detectors.
key_observables: Secret Key Rate (SKR), secure key distribution distance, counting rates ($Q[\mu,\mu]$), and bit error rates ($E_z$).
important_parameters: Distance (up to 303.57 km), detection efficiency ($\approx 55\%$), and the degree of State-Preparation Uncertainty (SPU).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the prepared states are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.), though the method is designed to handle general SPU forms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MDI-QKD setup, separate characterization schemes for phase and intensity, and plots showing the SKR versus transmission distance.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, describes the characterization of SPU sources, develops the theoretical framework using operator dominance, and presents the measured SKR results over increasing distances.
why_interesting: This work pushes the boundaries of practical quantum communication by providing a concrete, long-distance demonstration of QKD security under realistic, imperfect source conditions, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and quantum information theory.
